_why: The tabulating is trivial and none of these mutants touch it. Every one of them lets a pane survive the probe, and a leaked pane is not visible from the probe's own output — it shows up later as a polluted pane pool and a `pin-agents` run that resolves the wrong thing. The three escape routes a `trap` alone cannot cover are pinned separately: an exception (the `finally`), a signal (the installed handlers), and a create whose handle this process never learned (the journal's intent line).

mutations.name: intent-not-journalled-so-an-unnamed-pane-vanishes
mutations._mechanism: Stop recording the attempt before the create. A create that errors, hangs or is killed then leaves nothing in the journal, and the run reports `possible_leaks=0` — a clean bill of health for the one case where something may exist that this process never got to name. This is the window a trap structurally cannot close.

mutations.name: cleanup-skipped-on-the-normal-path
mutations._mechanism: The `finally` still runs, and closes nothing. Output is otherwise identical — the measurement is right, the summary prints `closed=0`, and every pane the probe made is still alive. Eight hand-rolled probes in one session is eight chances for this to go unnoticed until the pool is full.

mutations.name: resume-closes-nothing
mutations._mechanism: The recovery path becomes a no-op that reports success. It is the last line of defence — the one that covers a kill outrunning both the `finally` and the handlers — and it is exactly the path nobody exercises until they need it.
mutations.find:
closed, failed = close_all(journal, a.close)
        _, pending = journal.outstanding()
        print(f"CLEANUP: closed={closed} failed={len(failed)} possible_leaks={len(pending)}")
        return 0
mutations.replace:
closed, failed = 0, []
        _, pending = journal.outstanding()
        print(f"CLEANUP: closed={closed} failed={len(failed)} possible_leaks={len(pending)}")
        return 0

mutations.name: closes-not-recorded-so-resume-double-closes
mutations._mechanism: A handle stays in the journal forever, so every later `--resume` closes it again. By then the runtime may have reissued that handle to someone else's pane, and a cleanup tool that kills a stranger's terminal is worse than the leak it was written to fix.

mutations.name: signal-handlers-not-installed
mutations._mechanism: Default SIGTERM terminates the process without unwinding, so the `finally` never runs and every pane created so far is orphaned. Ctrl-C during a long probe is the single most likely way this tool ever exits early.
